facts.fact: Upon successful completion you earn the FMP-C credential — The Elite NP Functional Medicine Certification.
Fitzgerald Health Education Associates (FHEA) has partnered with The Elite Nurse Practitioner to offer this certification.
Program cost is $3,999 — a one-time fee for the full certification and 1-year access.

Affirm financing is available on FHEA. Exact monthly figures are computed by Affirm at checkout — quote only 'financing available via Affirm' plus an illustrative ballpark (~$334/mo over 12 months), always labeled illustrative.
facts.caution: never quote a fixed monthly price as fact

facts.fact: The program is accredited for 95 contact hours, including 24 Rx (pharmacology) hours that count toward prescribing requirements.
Elite NP partnered with NetCE for development; NetCE is an IACET Accredited Provider offering IACET CEUs compliant with the ANSI/IACET Continuing Education and Training Standard.
Completely online and self-paced — no travel or rigid schedules. 1 year to complete; most providers finish in 3–6 months.
You keep lifetime access to the core certification content available at the time of purchase, even after the certification year ends.
No prior functional medicine experience is needed — the program covers foundational concepts through advanced protocols.
Protocols are immediately applicable whether you work in primary care, urgent care, specialty clinics, or your own practice.
This certification is EXCLUDED from FHEA Memberships and must be purchased separately.
Program Director is Jenni Gallagher, MSN, NP-C — board-certified NP specializing in Functional Medicine, endocrinology, and metabolic health.

Course authors and SMEs: Brendan Tennefoss NP, Keri Douglas NP, Justin Groce NP, Haley Stevens NP, Lisa Vasile NP, Danielle Hawkins NP, Nicholas Goodwin (Psychiatric & Mental Health NP) — practicing NPs and functional-medicine specialists.

Curriculum modules: Legalities/Regulations/Risks; Foundations of Functional Medicine; Lab Interpretation in Functional Medicine; Gut Health and the Biome; Immunity and Inflammation; Sex Hormones; Cardiometabolic Health; Environmental Toxins; HPA Axis Dysregulation; Integrative Mental Health; Trauma/Stress/Mind-Body; Business & Practice Growth Strategies.
The Lab Interpretation module teaches tighter 'optimal' ranges vs conventional ones, functional markers beyond CBC/CMP, and pattern-based early-dysfunction detection driving personalized treatment.
Gut Health module: GI tract as epicenter of health/disease; dysfunction appearing as skin, brain, metabolic symptoms; treatment via digestion, absorption, elimination, microbiome pillars.

The Business & Practice Growth module teaches how to launch and scale a profitable functional-medicine clinic: cash vs insurance models, pricing, lab partnerships, patient retention, and marketing to attract cash-pay patients.
Path to certification: build foundations → master clinical & lab skills → demonstrate expertise via case studies and assessments → pass the exam → receive certification.

vs other programs: designed specifically for NPs; affordable and practical (no $20K+ price tags or unnecessary requirements); real-world clinical AND business strategies; completely online and self-paced.
Approximately 10,300+ U.S. clinicians hold a functional-medicine credential.
About 60 million chronically ill U.S. adults seek functional medicine.
Average annual earnings for functional-medicine providers: $221,000 (IQR $153k–$283k).
Legalities module: low-to-moderate liability, covered under malpractice insurance; treat within scope and refer when appropriate.

escalation: If a question cannot be answered from these facts (e.g., state-specific prescribing authority, employer reimbursement policy, medical advice), say so plainly and offer the human colleague — never guess.
